nba_directive.reason_text: This client is already engaged and asking about a refi — they don't need to be sold, they need a frictionless path forward. At 2.88%, today's rates almost certainly mean a higher payment, so the play is to respond directly and move them to the application step without over-pitching or stalling.
nba_directive.recommended_strategy_text:
- Reply immediately and directly to exactly what they asked — no generic opener, no re-pitch
  - Acknowledge their current situation: $314,077 balance, $1,508/mo P&I at 2.88% conventional
  - Do not lead with rate comparisons or savings claims — at 2.88%, today's market rates are likely higher, so let them drive the 'why'

- Ask the one clarifying question their request actually requires (if they haven't stated their goal)
  - One focused question only: 'Are you looking to pull cash out, shorten your term, or something else?' — this determines whether a refi pencils out for them
  - Do not stack additional discovery questions on top of this

- Move straight to the next step the moment their goal is clear
  - Offer the soft credit pull / pre-qualification link immediately: 'I can pull your numbers in under 10 minutes with no impact to your credit — want me to send the link now?'
  - If they're ready, send the e-sign or application link in the same message — remove every click of friction

- Avoid re-selling or piling on value statements they haven't asked for
  - Do not volunteer payment comparisons or break-even math unless they ask — at 2.88%, unsolicited math may kill momentum
  - Keep the reply short: direct answer + single next step

generated_sms: Hi there, great! I can send you a quick link to get started-it's a soft pull, no impact. Once that's in, I'll have your exact options ready. Sound good?

evaluation.comment: The model responded without violating policy. The response bore no relevance to the content of the prompt beyond the initial canned elements. CoT trace from the session review section shows that the "on rails" nature of the model is quite firm.
